# What Databricks OAuth client secrets the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every secret here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is thirty-two hexadecimal characters, so the run twice
# over is one, and the prefix in front brings a secret to thirty-six. Where a
# case turns on what a body may close on, it closes one on d instead.

patterns: databricks-oauth-client-secret

# The one prefix Databricks writes a secret with. There is a single kind of
# string here rather than a table of them: the secret a service principal is
# issued and the secret a registered OAuth application is given are the same
# string with no mark on it to tell one from another, so the cases below are that
# one shape in the places a secret is written.

case:     a secret in an environment assignment
in:       DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET=«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret in the profile the cli writes
in:       [DEFAULT]\nhost = https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com\nclient_secret = dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      [DEFAULT]\nhost = https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com\nclient_secret = «databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret in the body of a token request
in:       grant_type=client_credentials&scope=all-apis&client_secret=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      grant_type=client_credentials&scope=all-apis&client_secret=«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret on the command line a token request is made from
in:       curl -X POST -d client_id=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef -d client_secret=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/oidc/v1/token
out:      curl -X POST -d client_id=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef -d client_secret=«databricks-oauth-client-secret» https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/oidc/v1/token

case:     a secret in the property a jdbc connection takes it as
in:       jdbc:databricks://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com:443/default;OAuth2Secret=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      jdbc:databricks://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com:443/default;OAuth2Secret=«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret in the json the account api returns
in:       {"secret":"dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"secret":"«databricks-oauth-client-secret»"}

# The alphabet the thirty-two characters are written in: lowercase hexadecimal,
# which is what the scanner Databricks ships reads behind this prefix. The
# pattern's own file weighs the wider class a third-party ruleset reads instead —
# the letters, the digits, the underscore, the dot and the hyphen — and declines
# it; the last case here is why, since the prefix is a word and a hyphenated
# phrase reaches the count as readily as a secret does.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       dose0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dose0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     one uppercase character in a body
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF
out:      dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF

case:     a body carrying a letter outside hexadecimal
in:       dose0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying a dot
in:       dose0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       dose0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       dose0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef

case:     a hyphenated phrase reaching the count
in:       dose-response-curve-analysis-2024-v1
out:      dose-response-curve-analysis-2024-v1

# The lengths either side of thirty-two. Nothing is read behind that count, and
# it is used as a count rather than a floor: thirty-one characters are not a
# secret, and thirty-three are a secret and one character that belongs to no
# credential. The second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the
# match — a boundary there would drop this secret rather than trim it, and a real
# secret written against a letter would come through whole.

case:     a body of thirty-two characters is a secret
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a body of thirty-one characters is not
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     an alphabet run longer than a secret is a secret and what follows it
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»0

# What a secret may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a secret keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a secret after an underscore
in:       DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET_dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET_«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret after a letter
in:       xdose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a word written against a secret
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»suffix

case:     a secret at the end of a sentence
in:       the secret is dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the secret is «databricks-oauth-client-secret».

# Two secrets written together. A secret can begin inside another, and the s of
# the prefix is what bounds where: a candidate is found at that character and
# read back two places from it, and the only s a secret holds is the one its own
# prefix carries, so the positions inside one that could open a candidate are the
# last two characters of the body. The o of the prefix rules out the earlier of
# those two, since a candidate opening there would write that o as the last
# character of the body it stands in and no body holds an o — which is the third
# case here, where the secret is the one that prefix opens and the run in front
# of it stays. What is left is the second case, where the spans overlap and are
# redacted as one.

case:     two secrets with nothing between them
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefdose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a secret beginning at the last character of the secret before it
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdedose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a prefix written two characters from the end of a body
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcddose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       dose0123456789abcdose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dose0123456789abc«databricks-oauth-client-secret»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Thirty-two lowercase hexadecimal
# characters behind the prefix is the vendor's format exactly, and an MD5 is
# thirty-two of them, so the prefix written straight in front of one is a secret
# character for character and the whole of it goes. A longer digest is redacted
# for thirty-six characters with the rest left in the text. That is the answer
# rather than a fault in it, because nothing in the text tells such a run from a
# secret: sparing these would spare a real secret written the same way. What is
# taken is a stretch of a value that was already opaque.

case:     the prefix in front of an md5
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-1
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»01234567

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-256
in:       dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-oauth-client-secret»0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first two are the prefix, which is read
# in the case Databricks writes it and with every character of it; the third is a
# UUID, whose hyphens are no character a body may hold, so a hexadecimal run
# divided that way is no body however many characters it comes to. Then a word
# written against the prefix, whose body runs out at the first character
# hexadecimal has not got. The last three carry no prefix at all: a hexadecimal
# run holds neither the o nor the s, so no digest carries one partway along.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       DOSE0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DOSE0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix without its closing letter
in:       dos0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      dos0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       dose01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      dose01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a word written against the prefix
in:       dosedeadbeefcafe is no secret
out:      dosedeadbeefcafe is no secret

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a digest with no prefix
in:       md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# The values a secret is written beside, and the other credential Databricks
# issues. The client ID is a UUID the account console shows with the secret, the
# host is what the secret authenticates against, and a personal access token is
# written dapi and carries no dose to be found at — a credential this pattern's
# name does not cover rather than one the scan happens to miss.

case:     the client id a secret stands with
in:       DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     the workspace host a secret authenticates against
in:       DATABRICKS_HOST=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com
out:      DATABRICKS_HOST=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com

case:     a personal access token
in:       DATABRICKS_TOKEN=dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_TOKEN=dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line naming the endpoint a secret is exchanged at
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="requesting a token" url=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/oidc/v1/token
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="requesting a token" url=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/oidc/v1/token
